item.title: 北朝鮮、22日に改良型多連装ロケット砲を試射＝ＫＣＮＡ
item.description: [ソウル ２４日 ロイター] - 朝鮮中央通信
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ソウル ２４日 ロイター] - 朝鮮中央通信 （ＫＣＮＡ）は２４日、北朝鮮が２２日、改良型の２４０ミリ誘導多連装ロケット砲の試射を行ったと報じた。

ＫＣＮＡによると、今回の試射では、自律型精密誘導システムを採用した射程延伸型ロケットの精度と優位性が確認された。

ロケットは、通常の弾道飛行モードで１００キロ先、滑空を組み合わせた複合モードで１１５キロ先の目標を攻撃可能という。

ＫＣＮＡは、こうしたロケットの開発により、北朝鮮は南北境界線沿いの火力態勢に大きな変化をもたらすことになると伝えた。

試射を視察した朴正天（パク・ジョンチョン）朝鮮労働党中央軍事委員会副委員長は、最も殺傷力と破壊力の高い打撃戦力を南北境界線に集中させる必要性を強調したと、ＫＣＮＡは伝えた。

韓国国防省は、ロイターが電子メールで求めたコメント要請に直ちに応じなかった。

北朝鮮は、南北境界線付近に配備する意向の戦術兵器および通常兵器の増強を着実に進めている。

item.title: US, China agree to extend 'the Busan agreement' until January, Bessent says
item.description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Wednesday the United States and China agreed on Wednesday to extend "the Busan agreement."
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Wednesday the United States and China agreed on Wednesday to extend "the Busan agreement." His comments on Fox News' "Special Report" program came after he met with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping's state visit to Washington this week. "We met today to see if we could do a bigger deal as opposed to just a series of smaller things. We have agreed today that we will extend what we call the Busan Agreement," Bessent said, adding the agreement will be extended until January 10.

item.title: Barry Diller's People withdraws bid for MGM Resorts
item.description: Media mogul Barry Diller's People Inc on Wednesday withdrew its proposal to purchase all public shares of MGM Resorts International , sending the casino operator's shares down 8% in extended trading.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Media mogul Barry Diller's People Inc (PPLI.O) on Wednesday withdrew its proposal to purchase all public shares of MGM Resorts International (MGM.N) , sending the casino operator's shares down 8% in extended trading. In June, People, which currently owns about a 27% stake in MGM, had proposed to buy the remaining shares, valuing it at more than $18 billion. It had offered $48.30 a share in cash. People, formerly known as IAC, began building its stake in MGM in 2020, when the casino operator's shares were battered by closures and travel restrictions due to the COVID-19 pandemic. MGM owns marquee properties that account for roughly 40% of the Las Vegas Strip. It, however, has been struggling with sluggish footfalls, and has relied on growth in its China assets, including Macau, and digital operations in recent quarters. In a separate statement on Wednesday, MGM said the "board remains excited to continue to lead MGM Resorts as a standalone company." For Diller, who viewed MGM as undervalued, the increasing stake offered an opportunity for People to diversify beyond the core media business that includes publications such as its namesake magazine and Food & Wine magazine. "We didn't feel the mix was coming together in the way we had hoped and have decided not to pursue taking the company private at this time," Diller said. People, however, remains open to and interested in the possibility of a strategic transaction with MGM and looks forward to considering alternatives, he said. The media mogul's MGM pursuit echoes his earlier bet on travel and leisure through Expedia (EXPE.O) , which IAC acquired in 2002 before building and later spinning off the online travel company.

item.title: New College Swimming League dives into inaugural season with eye on wider audience
item.description: The new College Swimming League will launch its inaugural season on Thursday outside Chicago, seeking to give one of U.S. college sport's most successful but least visible disciplines a more prominent stage.
item.dc:creator: Rory Carroll
item.content:encoded: The new College Swimming League will launch its inaugural season on Thursday outside Chicago, seeking to give one of U.S. college sport's most successful but least visible disciplines a more prominent stage. The league, built in less than a year, brings together 12 programs from the SEC, ACC and Big Ten, three of the leading regional conferences in U.S. college sport, for a fall series of team competitions that will be streamed on ESPN platforms in the United States and shown internationally on DAZN. The opening match at FMC Natatorium in Westmont, Illinois, will feature Indiana, Louisville, Michigan and Ohio State. The eight-event season concludes with a championship in Indianapolis on Nov. 6. College Swimming League CEO Rob Kent said the venture was a calculated gamble, drawing on lessons from the [USN:L1N44M0ZP TEXT:"International Swimming League"] (ISL) while seeking to tap into the established fan bases of major universities. "There's only really two ways to do it," Kent told Reuters. "You either ease your way into it or you swing for the fences. And guess which side we took." LOOKING TO MAKE A SPLASH The competition will use a combined men's and women's team format, with four schools competing across 30 events in matches designed to last around two and a half hours. It will include spectator-friendly formats such as Skins, a multi-round elimination race, and a "jackpot" scoring rule that rewards dominant victories. Organizers hope the league can create a more compelling product for broadcasters and fans during a part of the college swimming calendar that has traditionally received limited attention. "We built it so that everybody here will go crazy, which looks really good on broadcast," Kent said, adding that the league was designed primarily with the television audience in mind. The field includes swimmers from more than 35 countries, including Virginia's Italian backstroke specialist [USN:L6N44A16O TEXT:"Sara Curtis"], who set the women's 50 metres backstroke world record in August. Tennessee's Jillian Crooks of the Cayman Islands and Michigan's Stephanie Balduccini of Brazil, both two-time Olympians, are also scheduled to compete. The league, which received funding from ISL founder and Ukrainian businessman Konstantin Grigorishin, will cover nearly $1 million in team travel costs and offer a $100,000 prize purse, with $25,000 going to each of the four schools that reach the championship. The money will go to athletic programs rather than directly to swimmers. Kent said direct athlete compensation was an ambition for the future, but that the first priority was establishing a viable commercial platform for swimmers whose sport has lagged football and basketball in exposure and revenue. "Student athletes that generate revenue should benefit," Kent said. "Swimming doesn't. So why don't we build something for them to do that? And here we are." COO and co-founder Kyle Sockwell said the league could increase athletes' visibility and help create opportunities for name, image and likeness (NIL) deals. "Your NIL just went from, for most of these swimmers, literally zero, to you might be able to get a sponsor because you're on a CSL team," Sockwell said. The top three teams will qualify automatically for the championship, while teams ranked fourth through seventh will compete for the final berth in a Nov. 5 Wild Card meet in Indianapolis.

item.title: Yohandy Morales HR carries Nationals past Tigers
item.description: Yohandy Morales hit a two-run homer and the visiting Washington Nationals held on for a 4-2 victory over the Detroit Tigers on Wednesday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Yohandy Morales hit a two-run homer and the visiting Washington Nationals held on for a 4-2 victory over the Detroit Tigers on Wednesday afternoon. Morales' fourth homer of the season allowed the Nationals (75-84) to win the three-game series 2-1. Brady House had two hits and scored a run while CJ Abrams, who homered twice on Tuesday, reached base three times and knocked in a run. Detroit starter Framber Valdez (10-12) gave up two runs and four hits while striking out six in 5 1/3 innings. Ben Malgeri hit his fifth homer of the season and drove in both Tigers runs. Kevin McGonigle added three hits for Detroit (74-85). Valdez set down the first 11 batters he faced before House slapped a single. Abrams drew a walk but Valdez got out of the jam by inducing Dylan Crews to ground out. Valdez walked two batters in the fifth but escaped again by striking out James Wood. Detroit also had two baserunners that inning as Zach McKinstry drew a two-out walk and McGonigle singled. They were left stranded as Hao-Yu Lee struck out. Washington broke the deadlock in the sixth. Andres Chaparro led off with a single and House followed with another hit. Abrams' single to right knocked in Chaparro and Morales' homer to right-center made it 3-0. Morales launched a Tyler Kinley slider an estimated 422 feet. Malgeri led off the bottom of the inning by launching the first pitch he saw from winning pitcher Will Dion (2-2) over the left-center field wall to put Detroit on the board. The Nationals manufactured a run in the seventh. Nasim Nunez singled, stole second and third and scored on Wood's groundout. Detroit threatened in the eighth as Riley Greene and Max Clark drew walks against Erik Tolman, but they were left stranded when Spencer Torkelson struck out against Yovanny Cruz, who came on after the walk to Clark. Singles by Jace Jung, McGonigle and Malgeri produced a ninth-inning run but Greene flied out to end the game as Cruz recorded his first save. --Field Level Media

item.title: Orioles win Game 1, eliminate Blue Jays from wild-card chase
item.description: Baltimore's Pete Alonso hit another home run and the Orioles eliminated the visiting Toronto Blue Jays from playoff contention by winning 4-2 on Wednesday afternoon in the first game of a doubleheader.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Baltimore's Pete Alonso hit another home run and the Orioles eliminated the visiting Toronto Blue Jays from playoff contention by winning 4-2 on Wednesday afternoon in the first game of a doubleheader. The Blue Jays (77-81) were the reigning American League champions, but they won't have a chance to return to the World Series. The Orioles (77-81) must win the nightcap of the day-night twinbill in order to stay alive for an AL wild-card spot, though if the Chicago White Sox win in Kansas City later Wednesday, that would bump Baltimore from contention. Chris Bassitt (9-5) pitched five-plus innings to notch a victory in his third consecutive start. He was charged with two runs on seven hits with one walk. Andrew Kittredge, the fourth reliever for the Orioles, worked the ninth for his 11th save. Max Scherzer (3-9) took the loss as he was charged with four runs and four hits in five innings. Ernie Clement and Andres Gimenez both had two hits, including a double each, for the Blue Jays. Toronto finished with 10 hits, leaving eight runners on base. The doubleheader was necessary after Tuesday night's scheduled game was postponed. Jeremiah Jackson's single gave Baltimore the game's first run in the second. Colton Cowser later scored when Jackson was caught attempting to steal second base. Alonso's two-run blast pushed the margin to 4-0 in the fifth inning. His 41st homer of the season was his third of the series, which began with his two-homer outing Monday night when the Orioles rallied for a 4-3 victory. Toronto scored two runs on the same play in the sixth inning, both charged to Bassitt. Brandon Valenzuela's two-out infield single pushed in a run and second baseman Jackson's throwing error allowed a second run to score. Alonso's homer was one of five Baltimore hits. The others were singles. The Orioles won Monday's game with six hits. Three Toronto relievers limited Baltimore to no runs with one hit. --Field Level Media

item.title: US FDA advisers endorse Grail cancer test's benefits in key vote
item.description: A panel of outside experts advising the US FDA said on Wednesday the benefits of Grail's blood-based cancer detection test outweigh its risks, paving the way for a potential landmark approval in cancer screening.
item.dc:creator: Padmanabhan Ananthan, Kamal Choudhury
item.content:encoded: A panel of outside experts advising the US FDA said on Wednesday the benefits of Grail's (GRAL.O) blood-based cancer detection test outweigh its risks, paving the way for a potential landmark approval in cancer screening. In a 7-2 vote with one abstention, the expert panel concluded that the test Galleri's ability to catch difficult-to-detect cancers justified its use in adults aged 50 and older. While the committee unanimously endorsed the test's safety, members split 6-4 on whether the evidence demonstrated its effectiveness. "This increases our confidence even more on FDA approval — almost derisked," Subbu Nambi, analyst at Guggenheim, said. "There is some debate about label, but we ultimately think FDA will approve for a wide range of cancers." The US Food and Drug Administration is not bound by its panel's votes but weighs them heavily when making final decisions. A final decision on whether Galleri can be sold nationwide is expected in the coming months. "By far, I think this is a paradigm shift," Dr. Marc Matrana, a medical oncologist at Ochsner MD Anderson Cancer Center and principal investigator on one of Grail's trials, had told Reuters before the meeting, citing strong patient interest. Galleri screens for multiple cancers from a single blood draw. In a US study, it detected 35% of cancers within 12 months and achieved a specificity of 99.85%. Results from a separate study in Britain were broadly consistent, reinforcing the test's low false-positive rate and cancer-detection capabilities. The committee also emphasized that doctors must clearly explain test limitations to patients so they do not skip proven screenings such as mammograms and colonoscopies, urging that Galleri must be an "addition, not substitution" to standard care. Both Grail's Galleri and Abbott's (ABT.N) Cancerguard are available to patients under Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments regulations, but neither of them is FDA-approved.

item.title: TBG prevê US$300 mi em reforços para atender térmicas do leilão de reserva
item.description: A Transportadora Brasileira Gasoduto Bolívia-Brasil (TBG) aguarda aval da Agência Nacional de Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis (ANP) para seguir adiante com investimentos de US$300 milhões necessários para atender uma demanda extra por gás do leilão de reserva de capacidade de março deste ano, afirmou o presidente, Jorge Hijjar, nesta quarta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Transportadora Brasileira Gasoduto Bolívia-Brasil (TBG) aguarda aval da Agência Nacional de Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis (ANP) para seguir adiante com investimentos de US$300 milhões necessários para atender uma demanda extra por gás do leilão de reserva de capacidade de março deste ano, afirmou o presidente, Jorge Hijjar, nesta quarta-feira. O aporte prevê obras em estações de compressão e reforços nos dutos e precisa ser empenhado até 2031, segundo o executivo da TBG, que tem a Petrobras como principal sócia, com 51% de participação. "Para que esse gás chegue a térmicas do leilão, a gente precisa de alguns reforços na malha; não muito grande, mas alguns reforços. E essa é uma definição que a ANP não pode demorar para (concluir), porque se ela demorar, a gente não consegue acabar para cumprimento do leilão", afirmou Hijjar. Os contratos no âmbito da TBG com usinas termelétricas a partir do leilão podem representar uma movimentação de aproximadamente 14 milhões de metros cúbicos de gás natural por dia (m³/dia).

item.title: Tesla's supervised self-driving system often misreads speed limits, Belgian safety group finds
item.description: Tesla’s FSD automated-driving system frequently exceeded speed limits and attempted to overtake cyclists on streets where it's prohibited, a road-safety advocacy group said, citing tests it conducted in Belgium.
item.dc:creator: Chris Kirkham, Marie Mannes
item.content:encoded: Tesla’s (TSLA.O) FSD automated-driving system frequently exceeded speed limits and attempted to overtake cyclists on streets where it's prohibited, a road-safety advocacy group said, citing tests it conducted in Belgium. The Belgian group Johanna.be - which advocates for pedestrian and cyclist safety - tested Tesla’s system over three days in July, covering about 400 km (249 miles). It found that FSD often exceeded speed limits in 20 km/h and 30 km/h zones, and incorrectly displayed higher speed limits to drivers, potentially misleading them about how fast the vehicle should travel. Tesla’s FSD driver-assistance feature can perform most driving tasks but requires drivers to pay strict attention. Dutch regulator RDW [USN:L1N40T0XG TEXT:"approved"] the system in April, with [USN:L1N41Q0KT TEXT:"Belgium"] and a handful of [USN:L8N45D165 TEXT:"other"] countries following suit. An EU-wide [USN:L6N41E0C3 TEXT:"vote"] could happen on October 6. Several EU countries, including Sweden, have [USN:L6N41E09R TEXT:"expressed concerns"] about FSD exceeding speed limits, while countries that approved it say drivers remain responsible for complying with traffic laws. Tesla and RDW did not respond to Reuters requests for comment. Tesla released a study earlier this month saying that FSD-enabled Teslas do not speed excessively and drive at speeds matching surrounding traffic. Xavier Lesenne, spokesperson for the Flemish government’s transportation ministry, which approved FSD in Belgium earlier this year, said it is "a learning system that continuously processes new and additional information" and adapts over time. Lesenne said the driver "remains 100% responsible" and must be ready to intervene "should the system make an error or fail to correctly apply a traffic rule." Lesenne said data from Tesla shows the technology "holds significant potential for accident prevention today." Johanna.be found that FSD exceeded the limit in the majority of the tested 30 km/h road segments around Brussels, averaging 44 km/h. Even though the vehicle's screen showed the system recognised 30 km/h speed-limit signs on the roadside, it often displayed an incorrect speed limit of 50 km/h. "It is akin to a passenger constantly reassuring the driver that the speed limit is 50 km/h in nearly every 30-zone through which they pass," the report said. Videos collected by the group show the FSD-enabled Tesla attempting to overtake cyclists on streets where doing so is not allowed. The European Transport Safety Council has previously raised concerns about whether FSD can comply with differing road rules across Europe. The Johanna.be report also noted positive aspects of the system, saying it "behaved cautiously and courteously around pedestrians and cyclists, often yielding proactively." But those benefits "do not offset the documented failures to comply with speed limits and cycle-street regulations." The NGO said it sent the report to the Flemish ministry and RDW, urging both to reassess the approvals.

item.title: Trump should press Xi to stop support for Iran, Democratic senator says
item.description: US Democratic Senator Jeanne Shaheen said on Wednesday President Donald Trump should press Chinese President Xi Jinping at a summit this week over China's support for Iran, saying that Chinese firms were helping Tehran economically and militarily.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US Democratic Senator Jeanne Shaheen said on Wednesday President Donald Trump should press Chinese President Xi Jinping at [USN:L6N45E02J TEXT:"a summit this week"] over China's support for Iran, saying that Chinese firms were helping Tehran economically and militarily. In a Senate speech, Shaheen cited reports that Iran obtained high-resolution satellite imagery of a base in Jordan from Chinese entities before launching a [USN:L6N45606R TEXT:"missile attack that killed three American soldiers"] and wounded four others. She noted that about 90% of Iran's oil exports go to China and provided it with "billions of dollars of revenue" and a "critical economic lifeline." Shaheen said Chinese and Hong Kong companies had also supplied components used in Iranian ballistic missiles and drones She urged Trump to "use his leverage" with Xi to stop Chinese firms from providing satellite imagery, missile and drone parts and access to markets for sanctioned Iranian oil. "If we want to bring this war to an end, we need to cut off the outside support that allows Iran to keep fighting, and that starts with China," she said. Shaheen said the administration should enforce sanctions against Chinese entities helping Iran, "and if China doesn't stop, Congress should impose additional consequences." She said Trump should also consider using authorities in recently enacted Russian sanctions legislation against Chinese purchasers of Russian energy, arguing that China was "the top funder of the war in Ukraine, as well as being one of the top funders of the war in Iran."

item.title: BC anuncia rolagem de swaps cambiais de novembro
item.description: O Banco Central informou nesta quarta-feira que dará início, em 5 de outubro, aos leilões para a rolagem dos swaps cambiais tradicionais que expiram em 3 de novembro.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O Banco Central informou nesta quarta-feira que dará início, em 5 de outubro, aos leilões para a rolagem dos swaps cambiais tradicionais que expiram em 3 de novembro. O BC informou em nota que poderá alterar o lote ofertado a cada dia, ou mesmo acatar propostas em montante inferior à oferta, conforme as condições de demanda pelo instrumento. De acordo com o BC, as condições de cada leilão serão anunciadas por meio de comunicado. No contrato de swap cambial tradicional, o título paga ao comprador a variação da taxa de câmbio acrescida de juros. Em troca, o BC recebe a variação da taxa Selic. A operação equivale à injeção de dólares no mercado futuro.

item.title: Washington lawyer Goldstein loses bid for release as he appeals tax crime conviction
item.description: Washington lawyer Tom Goldstein on Wednesday failed to convince a US appeals court to free him from jail as he fights to overturn his conviction and six-year prison sentence for tax and financial crimes stemming from his side career as a high-stakes poker player.
item.dc:creator: Mike Scarcella
item.content:encoded: Washington lawyer Tom Goldstein on Wednesday failed to convince a US appeals court to free him from jail as he fights to overturn his conviction and six-year prison sentence for tax and financial crimes stemming from his side career as a high-stakes poker player. In a brief order, the Richmond, Virginia-based 4th US Circuit Court of Appeals denied Goldstein's request to be released from custody. Goldstein, once one of the country’s top lawyers arguing cases before the US Supreme Court, was [USN:L6N43O0OQ TEXT:"sentenced in July"] following his conviction over allegations that he failed to report millions of dollars in poker winnings, lied on home mortgage loan documents and made improper payments through his former law firm. US District Judge Lydia Griggsby in the federal court in Greenbelt, Maryland, had allowed Goldstein to remain free during his trial but ordered him to begin serving his prison sentence immediately. Goldstein's lawyers and the US Attorney's Office for Maryland did not immediately respond to requests for comment. In a court filing, prosecutors called Goldstein "a flight risk with substantial international ties, including with a foreign billionaire who, in Goldstein’s view, is indebted to Goldstein for his own freedom." His lawyers countered that he has no intention of fleeing if released. Goldstein has argued Griggsby's instructions to jurors at the trial violated due process and “crippled” his defense strategy. He also argues that the trial court wrongly excluded some of his communication with third parties that he said contained evidence countering the government's assertion that he acted willfully to violate tax laws. In a court filing , his lawyers told the appeals court that "in this case, the government decided to secure a conviction no matter the facts or law." Goldstein argued more than 40 cases at the Supreme Court before retiring in 2023 and was a founder of the SCOTUSblog legal news website. He was charged in January 2025 with concealing earnings and losses from poker games in the United States and abroad with stakes reaching millions of dollars. A jury [USN:L6N3ZD0Y2 TEXT:"convicted"] Goldstein in February after a six-week trial. He [USN:L6N3Z80BS TEXT:"admitted"] at trial that he should have paid more attention to his tax returns but denied intentionally violating any laws. The case is United States v. Goldstein, 4th US Circuit Court of Appeals, No. 26-4392. For the United States: David Bornstein and Jason Poole of the Department of Justice For Goldstein: Elizabeth Prelogar of Cooley; and Jonathan Kravis of Liu Shur Kravis Read more: [USN:L6N43O0OQ TEXT:"Washington lawyer Tom Goldstein gets 6 years in prison for tax crimes"] [USN:L6N41Y173 TEXT:"Washington lawyer Goldstein hires ex-US solicitor general Prelogar to fight tax verdict"] [USN:L6N3ZD0Y2 TEXT:"Prominent Washington lawyer Tom Goldstein convicted at tax trial"] [USN:L6N3Z80BS TEXT:"Lawyer Tom Goldstein admits 'mistakes' but denies tax crimes at US trial"]

item.title: BC anuncia leilões de linha para quinta-feira no valor total de até US$1 bi
item.description: O Banco Central realizará na quinta-feira dois leilões de venda de dólares com compromisso de recompra no valor total de até US$1 bilhão, segundo comunicado divulgado pela autarquia nesta quarta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O Banco Central realizará na quinta-feira dois leilões de venda de dólares com compromisso de recompra no valor total de até US$1 bilhão, segundo comunicado divulgado pela autarquia nesta quarta-feira. As propostas serão acolhidas das 10h30 às 10h35. As operações de venda do BC serão liquidadas em 28 de setembro. Já as operações de compra estão divididas em duas datas: para o leilão A, a recompra ocorrerá em 2 de fevereiro de 2027, enquanto para o leilão B, a recompra se dará em 2 de abril de 2027.

item.title: UK Treasury open to smaller fiscal headroom to reduce tax hikes, FT reports
item.description: British finance minister John Healey may accept a smaller fiscal buffer to reduce tax rises in next month’s budget as investors signaled the gilt market would not be spooked by a more modest headroom target, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: British finance minister John Healey may accept a smaller fiscal buffer to reduce tax rises in next month’s budget as investors signaled the gilt market would not be spooked by a more modest headroom target, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday. The Treasury and Downing Street are debating whether to set a lower buffer in the budget than the government's fiscal watchdog forecast in [USN:L8N3ZR17W TEXT:"March"], the report said, citing people familiar with the discussions. One person involved in the government’s discussions suggested that headroom of £15 billion ($19.85 billion) would be enough, while another suggested closer to £20 billion, and a third person said no figure was yet being targeted, the report added. Healey, who is set to present his budget next month, is under [USN:L8N45E06Z TEXT:"pressure"] to show how he can meet his fiscal rules without raising the main taxes. The Treasury declined to comment on the report. ($1 = 0.7556 pounds)

item.title: Report: Giants OLB Brian Burns (ankle) out Sunday, but likely no surgery
item.description: New York Giants edge rusher Brian Burns likely will avoid surgery on his injured left ankle, but he is expected to miss Sunday's home game against the Tennessee Titans, ESPN reported.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New York Giants edge rusher Brian Burns likely will avoid surgery on his injured left ankle, but he is expected to miss Sunday's home game against the Tennessee Titans, ESPN reported. Giants coach John Harbaugh told reporters Wednesday that Burns is day-to-day. The Giants' initial injury report for the week said Burns did not participate in practice, but contained no injury designation. The ace pass rusher left Monday's 28-6 road loss to the Los Angeles Rams upon suffering the injury. He told reporters after the game that he suffered a low ankle sprain. "It eases my mind to know that it ain't nothing serious," Burns said. Burns, 28, registered two tackles and a quarterback hit against Los Angeles. The eight-year veteran has no sacks in the team's first two games after recording a career-high 16.5 last season. This is Burns' third season with the Giants after being acquired in a trade with the Carolina Panthers in March 2024. The Giants signed him to a five-year, $141 million contract soon after the trade. --Field Level Media

item.title: Trump abordará tema de detenidos con Xi; es posible que no se traten otras cuestiones relacionadas con derechos humanos
item.description: Se espera que el presidente Donald Trump presione al líder chino Xi Jinping para que libere a dos ciudadanos estadounidenses retenidos por China, pero no está claro si otros asuntos relacionadas con los derechos humanos recibirán la misma atención durante la cumbre de esta semana.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh, Jonathan Landay, Patricia Zengerle
item.content:encoded: Se espera que el presidente Donald Trump presione al líder chino Xi Jinping para que libere a dos ciudadanos estadounidenses retenidos por China, pero no está claro si otros asuntos relacionadas con los derechos humanos recibirán la misma atención durante la cumbre de esta semana. En un avance de la visita de Xi el pasado viernes, un funcionario estadounidense dijo que es probable que Trump plantee a Xi los casos de personas detenidas injustamente en China. Sin embargo, la Casa Blanca no ha confirmado si Trump abordará directamente asuntos más amplios relacionadas con los derechos humanos, como el Tíbet, la minoría musulmana uigur y la nueva ley de "unidad étnica" del país. Según los defensores de los derechos humanos, Trump ha convertido en una prioridad la liberación de los estadounidenses retenidos en el extranjero, incluida China. No obstante, el líder republicano ha evitado en gran medida hablar del historial de China en materia de derechos humanos y no ha planteado públicamente asuntos relacionadas con los derechos humanos en sus encuentros con otros líderes mundiales, como el primer ministro israelí, Benjamin Netanyahu; el príncipe heredero saudita, Mohamed bin Salman; y el primer ministro indio, Narendra Modi. Trump pedirá a Xi que libere a Youlin Chen, un experto de origen chino en pruebas nucleares norcoreanas que lleva encarcelado desde finales de 2024, y a Min Zin, un académico detenido en junio, según la esposa de Chen, Yufang Rong. Ambos son ciudadanos estadounidenses. Trump planteó el caso de Chen cuando se reunió con Xi en Pekín en mayo, pero no ha habido novedades desde entonces, dijo ella. "Esperamos que el doctor Chen y Zin puedan volver a casa tras esta reunión", dijo Elizabeth Richards, directora de investigación de la Fundación James Foley, una organización que defiende a los rehenes. Los grupos de derechos humanos y los parlamentarios demócratas afirman que Trump también debe presionar a Xi sobre el trato que China dispensa a los tibetanos y a los uigures, y alzar la voz en defensa de los manifestantes prodemocráticos de Hong Kong. Los demócratas del Congreso afirman que Trump está restando importancia a las preocupaciones en materia de derechos humanos y adoptando un enfoque transaccional en los asuntos internacionales. "No podemos abandonar los derechos humanos en nuestra política exterior», dijo el miércoles el legislador demócrata Jim McGovern, de Massachusetts. "El historial de China es indiscutible y atroz". Pekín ha dejado claro que este asunto estará fuera de los límites de la intermediación. El embajador de China en Estados Unidos advirtió el miércoles que la democracia y los derechos humanos son "líneas rojas" que no se pueden traspasar. Las organizaciones de derechos humanos afirman que China ha detenido a uigures con el pretexto de combatir el extremismo y los ha recluido en campos de reeducación. Secretarios de Estado estadounidenses de ambos partidos han calificado el trato a los uigures de genocidio. "La visita de Xi a Washington es un momento estratégico para ir más allá de las palabras de condena sobre el genocidio uigur», dijo Turgunjan Alawdun, presidente del Congreso Mundial Uigur. La embajada de China en Washington no respondió a una solicitud de comentarios. Pekín afirma que ha establecido "centros de formación profesional" para frenar el extremismo y niega las acusaciones de abusos. Las organizaciones de derechos humanos y los exiliados también suelen calificar el dominio de China en el Tíbet de "opresivo", una acusación que Pekín rechaza. China ha ejercido un mayor control sobre la región desde que Xi asumió la dirección del Partido Comunista en 2012. Pekín afirma que Washington debería dejar de utilizar "los asuntos relacionadas con el Tíbet para interferir en los asuntos internos de China".

item.title: Rangers F Adam Sykora (lower-body injury) out for 4-5 months
item.description: New York Rangers forward Adam Sykora will miss four to five months because of a lower-body injury.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New York Rangers forward Adam Sykora will miss four to five months because of a lower-body injury. Sykora, 22, was injured in the first period of the Rangers' 3-2 preseason loss to the host New Jersey Devils on Monday. He was off balance when he took a hit in the corner from Devils defenseman Mikael Diotte and fell awkwardly into the boards. Sykora needed assistance from teammates and a trainer to get off the ice. Considered a promising prospect, Sykora played in 11 games for the Rangers last season and had three goals, one assist, a zero plus-minus rating, five penalty minutes, 10 blocks and 20 hits in 11:10 average ice time. The Slovakia native had 29 points (12 goals, 17 assists) in 62 games last season with Hartford of the American Hockey League. The Rangers selected Sykora in the second round of the 2022 NHL Draft. New York opens the regular season on Tuesday against the host Boston Bruins. --Field Level Media

item.title: North Korea conducted test of upgraded rocket launcher system, KCNA says
item.description: North Korea conducted a test firing of an upgraded 240mm guided multiple rocket launcher system on Tuesday, state news agency KCNA reported on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: North Korea conducted a test firing of an upgraded 240mm guided multiple rocket launcher system on Tuesday, state news agency KCNA reported on Thursday. The test proved the accuracy and superiority of the range-extended rockets, which use an autonomous precision guidance system, KCNA said. The rockets are able to strike targets 100 km (62 miles) away in a trajectory flight mode and 115 km away in a combined glide mode, it added. The development of such rockets assures North Korea of a significant change in the firepower readiness along the southern border, the news agency said, effectively referring to the one it shares with South Korea. Pak Jong-chon, vice-chairman of the Central Military Commission who oversaw the test, stressed the need to concentrate the deadliest and most destructive attack forces on the southern border, KCNA said. South Korea's defense ministry did not immediately respond to an emailed Reuters request for comment Pyongyang has been steadily upgrading its tactical and conventional arsenal that it intends to deploy near the border with South Korea. In June, North Korean leader Kim Jong Un [USN:L1N42X18G TEXT:"oversaw tests"] of key weapons, including an upgraded rocket launcher and tactical missiles, that the country said would also be used to defend its southern border.

item.title: Senators from both parties ask Trump to release emergency heating oil as prices surge
item.description: The two US senators from Maine, the state most reliant on home heating oil, asked President Donald Trump this week to tap the country's emergency stash of the fuel as diesel prices soar to record levels and push up household bills.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The two US senators from Maine, the state most reliant on home heating oil, asked President Donald Trump this week to tap the country's emergency stash of the fuel as diesel prices soar to record levels and push up household bills. "We write to request that you release home heating oil from the Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve to protect Mainers from the very high prices that are imposing a difficult financial burden," Senators Susan Collins, a Republican, and Angus King, an independent who caucuses with Democrats, wrote in a letter to Trump on Tuesday. Collins, who is in a tight race for her seat in the November midterm elections, told Reuters in a statement the cost of energy is a "huge issue in my state" and that tapping the reserve "would help put downward pressure on prices." Maine households are paying about $675 more to fill a heating oil tank than they did last year, the senators said, citing a Maine Department of Energy Resources survey. Prices for diesel, which is similar to heating oil, have surged to a record over $6.50 a gallon as the wars in Iran and Ukraine have crimped production of fuels and petroleum shipments. The White House did not immediately respond to a query about the letter. Collins also joined Senator Jack Reed, a Democrat of Rhode Island, in asking the administration to release home heating program money to help low-income households. The reserve, which stores 1 million barrels of diesel in four sites from Maine to New Jersey, was created in 2000 by former President Bill Clinton. It holds roughly 10 days of heating oil for the region and has not been tapped since 2012, when it provided fuel to emergency responders in the aftermath of Hurricane Sandy. Trump's budget last year [USN:L2N3S50K0 TEXT:"proposed to shut"] the reserve, which is expensive to maintain. The soaring diesel price has spurred calls for a ban on exports of the fuel, but the White House on Wednesday [USN:L1N45F0S9 TEXT:"denied"] a news report that said the administration is preparing a 90-day ban on diesel exports.

item.title: Trump abordará questão de detidos com Xi, mas outros temas relacionados a direitos humanos podem não ser discutidos
item.description: O presidente norte-americano, Donald Trump, deve pressionar o líder chinês, Xi Jinping, a libertar dois cidadãos norte-americanos detidos pela China, mas não está claro se outras questões relacionadas aos direitos humanos receberão atenção semelhante durante a cúpula desta semana.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh, Jonathan Landay, Patricia Zengerle
item.content:encoded: O presidente norte-americano, Donald Trump, deve pressionar o líder chinês, Xi Jinping, a libertar dois cidadãos norte-americanos detidos pela China, mas não está claro se outras questões relacionadas aos direitos humanos receberão atenção semelhante durante a cúpula desta semana. Em uma antecipação da visita de Xi na última sexta-feira, uma autoridade norte-americana afirmou que Trump provavelmente abordará com Xi os casos de pessoas detidas injustamente na China. No entanto, a Casa Branca não informou se Trump levantará diretamente questões mais amplas relacionadas aos direitos humanos no Tibete, à minoria muçulmana uigur e à nova lei de “unidade étnica” do país. Trump tem feito da conquista da liberdade para os norte-americanos detidos no exterior uma prioridade, inclusive na China, afirmam defensores dos direitos humanos. Mas o líder republicano tem evitado, em grande parte, falar sobre o histórico de direitos humanos da China e não levantou publicamente questões de direitos humanos ao se reunir com outros líderes mundiais, como o primeiro-ministro israelense, Benjamin Netanyahu, o príncipe herdeiro saudita, Mohammed bin Salman, e o primeiro-ministro indiano, Narendra Modi. Trump pedirá a Xi que libere Youlin Chen, nascido na China, especialista em testes nucleares norte-coreanos que está preso desde o final de 2024, e Min Zin, um acadêmico preso em junho, segundo a esposa de Chen, Yufang Rong. Ambos são cidadãos norte-americanos. Trump levantou o caso de Chen quando se encontrou com Xi em Pequim em maio, mas nada aconteceu desde então, disse ela. “Esperamos ver o dr. Chen e Zin voltarem para casa após essa reunião”, disse Elizabeth Richards, diretora de pesquisa da Fundação James Foley, um grupo de defesa de reféns. Grupos de direitos humanos e parlamentares democratas afirmam que Trump também precisa pressionar Xi sobre o tratamento dado pela China aos tibetanos e uigures e defender os manifestantes pró-democracia de Hong Kong. Os democratas no Congresso afirmam que Trump está minimizando as preocupações com os direitos humanos e adotando uma abordagem transacional nas relações internacionais. “Não podemos abandonar os direitos humanos em nossa política externa”, disse nesta quarta-feira o deputado democrata Jim McGovern, de Massachusetts. “O histórico da China é indiscutível e é atroz.” Pequim tem sinalizado que o tema estará fora de discussão. O embaixador do país nos EUA advertiu nesta quarta-feira que democracia e direitos humanos são “linhas vermelhas” que não podem ser ultrapassadas. Grupos de direitos humanos afirmam que a China deteve uigures sob o pretexto de combater o extremismo e os confinou em campos de reeducação. Secretários de Estado dos EUA de ambos os partidos classificaram o tratamento dado aos uigures como genocídio. “A visita de Xi a Washington é um momento estratégico para ir além das palavras de condenação ao genocídio uigur”, disse o presidente do Congresso Mundial Uigur, Turgunjan Alawdun. A embaixada da China em Washington não respondeu a um pedido de comentário. Pequim afirma ter estabelecido “centros de formação profissional” para coibir o extremismo e nega as acusações de abusos. Grupos de direitos humanos e exilados também costumam descrever o domínio da China no Tibete como “opressivo”, uma acusação que Pequim rejeita. A China tem exercido maior controle sobre a região desde que Xi assumiu a liderança do Partido Comunista em 2012. Pequim afirma que Washington deveria parar de usar “questões relacionadas ao Tibete para interferir nos assuntos internos da China”. A Campanha Internacional pelo Tibete pediu a Trump que solicitasse a Xi “a retomada de um diálogo substantivo, sem precondições”, com o Dalai Lama, líder espiritual dos budistas tibetanos e ganhador do Prêmio Nobel da Paz. O Departamento de Estado reiterou os apelos por tal diálogo quando um tibetano-americano morreu após se imolar em julho. A China aprovou uma lei este ano para criar uma identidade nacional comum entre os 55 grupos étnicos minoritários do país, que inclui penalidades para pessoas fora do país por “incitar o separatismo étnico”. O Departamento de Estado considera a lei problemática. Katie LaRoque, diretora de políticas e defesa da Freedom House, instou Trump a condenar pessoalmente a legislação. “O presidente Trump precisa deixar claro que a legislação interna de Pequim não tem jurisdição sobre aqueles que exercem suas liberdades fundamentais em solo americano”, afirmou ela.

item.title: US pledges $267 million more to fight Ebola in central Africa
item.description: The US State Department on Wednesday pledged an additional $267 million toward fighting the Ebola outbreak in central Africa, as health authorities battle to get the deadly virus under control.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US State Department on Wednesday pledged an additional $267 million toward fighting the Ebola outbreak in central Africa, as health authorities battle to get the deadly virus under control. Senior State Department officials announced the funding on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, where they hoped other countries would pledge new funds toward a target of $2 billion to deal with the disease, mainly in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The outbreak was detected in May and is already the [USN:L6N44E0K6 TEXT:"second most lethal"] on record, behind one in West Africa from 2014 to 2016. The pledge brings the Trump administration's commitment to tackling the outbreak to $886 million, including $107 million from the Department of Health and Human Services in addition to State Department funding. The assistance would help countries contain the outbreak at its source, one of the officials said, such as for building treatment facilities, providing diagnostics and medical countermeasures for health workers in the field.

item.title: 賃金に大きな上昇圧力見られず、インフレ高進も＝ＥＣＢレーン専務理事
item.description: [ローザンヌ（スイス） ２３日 ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）のチーフエコノミストであるフィリップ・レーン専務...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
賃金に大きな上昇圧力見られず、インフレ高進も＝ＥＣＢレーン専務理事 6:18 配信

欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）のチーフエコノミスト、フィリップ・レーン専務理事。英ロンドンで６月撮影。REUTERS/Chris J. Ratcliffe

[ローザンヌ（スイス）　２３日　ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）のチーフエコノミストであるフィリップ・レーン専務理事は、今年のエネルギー価格高騰によるインフレ高進を受けても、賃金への大きな上昇圧力は見られていないとし、急速な物価上昇が定着する恐れがあるとの懸念を打ち消した。

レーン氏はスイスの大学での講演で、「エネルギーショックに対する大きな反応は見られない」とした上で、「人々は生活費が予想以上に上昇していることを認識している一方で、多くの企業が『中国に競争で負けている。あまりに高い賃上げを求められるなら、いつでも人工知能（ＡＩ）を導入できる』と考えている」状況が背景にあるとの見方を示した。

８月のユーロ圏消費者物価指数（ＨＩＣＰ）速報値は、エネルギーコストの上昇を背景に再び３％を超えた。一部のエコノミストは、中東情勢の緊迫化を背景に燃料・ガス価格がここ数週間で急騰していることから、年末までに４％に達するとみている。エネルギー価格の急騰を受け、市場はＥＣＢが６月と９月の利上げに加え、さらに３回から４回の追加利上げに踏み切るとの見方を織り込んでいる。

ただ、市場データから上乗せ金利（リスクプレミアム）を除けば、政策金利のピークは来年に３％をやや上回る水準に達し、同年末までに低下する見通しで、実際には追加利上げ２回分しか織り込まれていないとレーン氏は指摘。一方、エネルギー価格は来年半ばまでＥＣＢの「不利なシナリオ」に沿って推移し、その後にようやく基準シナリオの水準に戻ると見込まれており、これがリスク要因になっていると認めた。

レーン氏はまた、天然ガスの在庫不足もリスクだと指摘。エネルギー企業が夏場にガスの備蓄を先送りしたため、備蓄水準は７０％にとどまり、過去の平均を１６％ポイント下回っている。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：ＥＣＢ「予防的」追加利上げへ、米イラン紛争長期化で アングル：ＥＣＢ、金利据え置きへ　原油価格が再び焦点 アングル：ＡＩの経済金融への影響、ＥＣＢフォーラムで希望と懸念が交錯 アングル：金融市場はＥＣＢのタカ派化見込む、イラン戦による油価高騰で コラム：求むＥＣＢ総裁、危機に強い革新者 最終更新: 9/24(木) 6:18 ロイター

item.title: ロシア、プーチン氏のＧ２０出席検討 米が招請＝大統領府報道官
item.description: [２３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[２３日　ロイター] - ロシアのペスコフ大統領報道官は２３日、米国で今年開催される主要２０カ国・地域（Ｇ２０）首脳会議に関し、ルビオ米国務長官がプーチン大統領に出席を招請したことについて、ロシア側として検討する考えを示した。ロシア通信各社がペスコフ氏の発言として伝えた。

ペスコフ氏は「メディアの報道と国務長官の発言を確認した。この招請に謝意を表する」と表明。「われわれは決定を下し、外交ルートを通じて対応していく」と述べた。

ルビオ長官は２３日、ロシアのラブロフ外相とのニューヨークでの会談後、プーチン大統領がＧ２０首脳会議への招待を受け入れることを期待するとし、プーチン氏が出席すればトランプ米大統領と会談する機会になるとの認識を示した。

Ｇ２０首脳会議は１２月に米フロリダ州で開催される予定。

item.title: Arizona sues kratom drink maker for false advertising
item.description: Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes on Wednesday sued drink maker Botanic Tonics LLC, saying the company illegally sold kratom and kava tonics as "energy drinks" without disclosing the products' risks of addiction and withdrawal.
item.dc:creator: Dietrich Knauth
item.content:encoded: Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes on Wednesday sued drink maker Botanic Tonics LLC, saying the company illegally sold kratom and kava tonics as "energy drinks" without disclosing the products' risks of addiction and withdrawal. Botanic Tonics sells drinks under the "Feel free" brand in Arizona, and it is marketed as a wellness tonic, energy drink and a healthier alternative to alcohol. "Feel free" contains the psychoactive substance kratom, which has opioid-like qualities and is known colloquially as "gas station heroin," according to the lawsuit. Botanic Tonics markets the drinks to youth and its advertising obscures the drinks' kratom content, according to the lawsuit. Botanic Tonics did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Arizona had 146 kratom-related deaths from 2020 to 2023, according to the attorney general. Kratom is legal under federal law, but the US Drug Enforcement Administration moved to [USN:L4N4331MA TEXT:"restrict"] higher-concentration kratom products earlier this year. Texas, Missouri and the city of Baltimore have also filed lawsuits against companies that sell kratom products.

item.title: ＣＮＮなどのホワイトハウス排除措置、過去の判例に適合せず＝米地裁判事
item.description:
Jan Wolfe Jack Queen
[ワシントン ２３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Jan Wolfe　Jack Queen

[ワシントン ２３日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領が米メディアのＣＮＮ、ＭＳＮＯＷ（旧ＭＳＮＢＣ）、ポリティコの報道に不満を示し、３社の取材記者をホワイトハウスから締め出した措置について、連邦地裁判事は２３日の審理で、連邦控訴裁のこれまでの判例に適合していないように見えるとの見解を示した。ただ、報道機関側が求めているホワイトハウスへのアクセス回復については判断を下さなかった。

トランプ氏が１８日に３社をホワイトハウスから締め出すと表明したことを受け、３社は２１日、合衆国憲法修正第１条で保障された言論・報道の自由を侵害しているとしてトランプ政権を提訴した。

首都ワシントンの連邦地裁で開かれた審理では、３社が起こした訴訟の審理が続く間、ホワイトハウスへのアクセスを暫定的に回復するよう求める一時的差し止め命令の申し立てが検証された。３社はトランプ氏の措置は憲法修正第１条に違反するほか、適正手続き（デュー・プロセス）を受ける権利も侵害していると主張している。

連邦地裁のケリー判事は、コロンビア特別区連邦控訴裁判所の２件の判例で、ホワイトハウスの記者証を取り消される前に記者に適正手続きが保障されなくてはならないことが明確に示されていると指摘。ホワイトハウスは３社に対し、アクセス権剥奪に異議を申し立てる実質的な機会を与えていなかったように見えると述べた。

ケリー判事は「政府はこれらの判例は誤って判断されたものだと主張した」とし、「誤りだったかどうかは別として、判事である私はこれらの判例を適用しなければならない。控訴裁の判例で示されている手続きが今回は踏まれていなかったといえる」と指摘。一時差し止め命令の申し立てについては、後日判断を示す考えを示した。

この件を巡っては、報道の自由を擁護する団体連合と多数の報道機関がこの日、ＣＮＮ、ＭＳＮＯＷ、ポリティコを支持する法廷意見書を提出。「報道機関や記者が持つ権利を編集上の論調に対する認識を理由に剥奪することは、連邦最高裁の数十年にわたる判例に反し、ホワイトハウスを含むいかなる場においても許されない」とした。

意見書には、ロイター、ワシントン・ポスト紙、フォックス・ニュースのほか、報道の自由記者委員会（Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press）などが名を連ねている。

item.title: US judge steps aside in dispute over Hawaii energy settlement
item.description: A federal judge in Hawaii has disqualified himself from hearing a dispute over whether a decades-old price-fixing settlement bars the state from suing Chevron and other energy companies over climate change, concluding that he has a potential conflict of interest as a Hawaiian resident.
item.dc:creator: Mike Scarcella
item.content:encoded: A federal judge in Hawaii has disqualified himself from hearing a dispute over whether a decades-old price-fixing settlement bars the state from suing Chevron and other energy companies over climate change, concluding that he has a potential conflict of interest as a Hawaiian resident. In an order on Tuesday , US District Judge Micah Smith withdrew from further participation in the litigation, leading the court's chief judge to assign Oregon-based US District Judge Michael Mosman to take over. Smith, who joined the bench in 2023, said he and members of his family lived in Hawaii during the 1990s and might qualify as parties covered by the statewide settlement. “This conflict almost certainly extends, in one way or another, to all other district judges in the District of Hawai'i,” Smith wrote. Smith did not immediately respond to a request for comment left with his office. Chevron did not immediately respond to a request for comment, and Hawaii referred to its court submissions. In court filings, Chevron and Hawaii said they saw no need for Smith to recuse himself. The underlying lawsuit, filed by the state in 1998 on behalf of Hawaii residents, accused a group of energy companies of price-fixing and deceptive marketing. The case later settled for $35 million. Chevron and the other defendants denied wrongdoing. Earlier this year, Chevron and the other defendants asked Smith to enforce the settlement by blocking Hawaii from pursuing certain climate-related claims alleging the deceptive manufacturing, marketing and sale of petroleum products. The companies contend the settlement bars the related litigation that Hawaii is pursuing in state court. Before issuing his recusal ruling, Smith asked the Judicial Conference of the United States' Committee on Codes of Conduct for ethics guidance. The committee told Smith that because the case was brought on behalf of Hawaii residents under a federal antitrust statute, the judge and his wife have a "financial interest in the subject matter" of the action. But the committee said there were steps he could take to avoid recusal. Smith said he could not avoid the conflict of interest because he had already spent a substantial amount of time on the matter and because obtaining ethics waivers would be impractical. The case is Anzai v. Chevron Corp, US District Court for the District of Hawaii, No. 1:98-cv-00792. For plaintiffs: Vic Sher and Matthew Edling of Sher Edling For Chevron: Theodore Boutrous Jr of Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher; Anthony Dick of Jones Day; and Andrea Smith of Paul Weiss Read more: [USN:L1N42B12H TEXT:"US judicial panel tightens corporate disclosure rules to ensure judge recusals"] [USN:L2N3PF0XB TEXT:"US judge rejects request to recuse from case over courtroom pronoun policy"] [USN:L1N3X00XW TEXT:"US DOJ's misconduct complaint against judge in transgender military ban case gets tossed"] [USN:L2N3VJ0OF TEXT:"Judge recuses himself from Oregon National Guard case"] [USN:L1N3UJ024 TEXT:"US judge recuses herself from black-market drug case over Gilead stock purchases"]

item.title: Trading Day: US yields cross 5% threshold
item.description: US bond yields soared on Wednesday, in many cases to the highest since 2007, and expectations of an interest rate hike next month surged, after figures showed that US business activity is expanding at its fastest pace in more than five years.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded:
US bond yields soared on Wednesday, in many cases to the highest since 2007, and [USN:S0N4490DT TEXT:"expectations"] of an interest rate hike next month surged, after figures showed that US [USN:ZON00GJOX TEXT:"business activity"] is expanding at its fastest pace in more than five years. The sharp rise in market borrowing costs, and higher oil prices, pushed [USN:L6N45F0EX TEXT:"stocks"] into the red. In [USN:L6N45E0W6 TEXT:"my column today"], I look at the risk to ordinary investors posed by the record concentration of US stock market value in AI and 'tech-adjacent' companies. Passively managed index tracker funds are essentially tech funds now. Today's Key Reads [USN:L1N45F09P TEXT:"Pezeshkian says Iran won't surrender, after Trump's annihilation threat "] [USN:ZON00GJOX TEXT:"US business activity at more than five-year high; inflation pressures building"] [USN:L6N45915R TEXT:"There's a reason Trump is the only one talking about 1% interest rates"] Darkest before dawn? Funds mull return to bonds: Mike Dolan [USN:L6N45E0T3 TEXT:"Trump's diesel export dilemma — Good politics, bad economics: Bousso"] Today's Key Market Moves STOCKS: Wall Street down: Dow -0.7%, S&P 500 -0.8%, Nasdaq -1.1%. [USN:L4N45F0EL TEXT:"Europe"] -0.4%. SECTORS/SHARES: Every sector on the S&P 500 falls except energy, which rises 1%. Comms services, utilities -2%. Expedia, Airbnb -8%. Booking Holdings, McDonald's -5%. Palo Alto Networks, CrowdStrike Holdings +5%. FX: [USN:L4N45F01K TEXT:"Dollar"] leaps 0.5% to highest in nearly 2 months. Dollar/yen above 158.00. BONDS: French 10y 4.60%, US 10y 5.10%, highest since 2007-08. Extremely weak US 5y auction - lowest demand since 2018. COMMODITIES/METALS: [USN:L4N45F015 TEXT:"Oil"] snaps 5-day losing streak, Brent +4%, WTI +2%. [USN:L6N45F0ZY TEXT:"US diesel"] futures -2% to 2-week low. [USN:L4N45F01C TEXT:"Gold"] -1.5%.

Today's Talking Points: 'Risk free' 5% The yield on every US Treasury note or bond, with the exception of the two-year note, traded [USN:L8N45E1BK TEXT:"above 5%"] on Wednesday, with the five-year yield crossing that threshold for the first time since 2007. The two-year yield is only 5 basis points away, so it's conceivable that the whole US Treasury yield curve could be above 5% later this week. That would also be a first since 2007. It's only a number, but it could have psychological significance. It could tempt all kinds of investors to diversify away from expensive stocks and lock in attractive returns on 'risk-free' assets (the real yield on 10-year TIPS is 2.78%, the highest since 2008). On the other hand, today's 5-year auction was awful. These yields are a reminder that we are in a brave new world, where the cost of capital is high and seemingly heading higher. Debt servicing — for consumers, businesses and the Treasury — is getting more expensive. Buckle up. Here Xi comes Chinese President Xi Jinping arrives in Washington for his summit on Thursday with US President Donald Trump . The visit will be marked with [USN:L6N45E02J TEXT:"pomp, pageantry and platitudes"], but will it yield much else? Investors' expectations are low, but Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent indicated on Wednesday that there may be some [USN:S0N43U01A TEXT:"progress on trade."] Bessent said the US is open to extending the trade truce that expires on November 10 or considering a possibly larger trade deal, without giving details, other than it was the Chinese delegation's proposal. If Trump and Xi reach agreement on trade, there's unlikely to be much [USN:L6N45C084 TEXT:"cooperation on AI"]. Mutual trust is low, and neither side wants to slow down development. Diesel down US diesel futures slid 2% on Wednesday to a two-week low, reacting to comments from Trump the day before that he backs a ban on US diesel exports as a way to cool record high prices at the pump. Politico also reported that the administration was preparing a 90-day ban, which a White House official denied. Confused? Trump will no doubt be desperate to get diesel prices down, especially ahead of the US midterm elections in November . But while an export ban might play well politically, it [USN:L6N45E11V TEXT:"may not have the desired effect"], as it could push US refineries to cut the amount of crude they process, which would reduce the amount of gasoline and other products produced, which could raise prices. What could move markets tomorrow?
